name: Stir-Fry Week
summary: Hot wok, lots of vegetables: chicken and cashew, black pepper beef and broccoli, garlic shrimp and snow peas, and garlic-chili tofu with greens, all over brown rice or whole-wheat noodles in modest portions. Salmon three times, three dinners that make tomorrow's lunch, and no deep-frying.
howItWorks:
**Hot wok, real portions.** Dinners and most lunches are stir-fries or noodle dishes, cooked fast with a little oil, reduced-sodium soy sauce, low-sodium stock and a splash of rice vinegar. Rice is brown and the noodles are whole-wheat spaghetti, kept modest beside plenty of vegetables, beans or tofu. Sauces reduce in the pan, with a pinch of cornstarch in four of them so they cling.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's garlic-chili tofu, Tuesday's chicken and cashew and Wednesday's black pepper beef each make two portions, so the next lunch is done. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep it up to 3 days, pack it cold for work and reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

**Fish and protein.** Canned salmon on Monday, then fresh salmon on Friday and Sunday, bring omega-3 and **vitamin D**. Shrimp, beef, chicken, tofu, edamame, chickpeas and eggs cover the rest, with eggs at three breakfasts, one snack and two dishes. Cook fresh salmon and shrimp within a day of buying, and thaw frozen shrimp in the fridge.

**What changes with size.** Light starts from smaller portions of rice, noodles, meat, fish, tofu, nuts, oil and honey, with no snack on four days and one on the other three. Big adds a snack on six days (a pineapple and pear cup on Thursday), swaps Thursday's yogurt bowl for oatmeal, and grows the rice, noodles, protein and beans.

recipes.name: Orange-ginger oatmeal with nuts and pumpkin seeds
recipes.about: Creamy oatmeal cooked in milk with a little fresh ginger and cinnamon, topped with a spoonful of Greek yogurt, juicy orange segments, toasted walnuts, almonds and pumpkin seeds. The oats and seeds bring **fibre, iron and magnesium**, the almonds bring vitamin E, the walnuts bring omega-3 fats, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, then peel it and cut it into segments. Toast the walnuts, almonds and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until the pumpkin seeds puff and pop, about 3 minutes.
Stir the oats, milk, grated ginger, cinnamon and a splash of water together in a small pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the yogurt, orange segments, nuts and pumpkin seeds.
recipes.tip: Make it the night before: soak the oats in the milk in the fridge, then warm it in the morning. Eat soaked oats within 3 days.

recipes.name: Pineapple yogurt bowl with toasted oats and nuts
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt with sweet pineapple, a drizzle of honey, and a crunchy topping of toasted oats, almonds and walnuts. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the nuts bring vitamin E and omega-3 fats.

ingredients.note: peeled, cored and cut into small chunks

steps: Toast the oats, almonds and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until golden and fragrant, about 4 minutes. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Wash the pineapple before cutting, then cut it into small chunks. Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the pineapple.
Scatter over the crunchy topping and drizzle with the honey.
recipes.tip: Toast a few days of the oat topping at once and keep it in a jar.

recipes.name: Tomato and scallion egg scramble with spinach on whole-wheat toast
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese tomato and egg stir-fry
recipes.about: Eggs scrambled until completely firm with juicy tomato, scallion and a handful of spinach, piled on whole-wheat toast with a little soy and sesame, with a glass of milk and an orange on the side. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the spinach and tomato bring folate and vitamin C.

ingredients.note: washed, peeled and cut into segments, on the side

steps: Wash the tomato, spinach, scallion and orange, then chop the tomato and slice the scallion. Beat the eggs with the soy sauce. Peel the orange and cut it into segments.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the tomato and most of the scallion until the tomato softens and the juices thicken, about 3 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently until completely set and no wet egg remains, about 2 minutes.
Pile onto the toast, drizzle with the sesame oil, scatter over the rest of the scallion and serve with the orange and a glass of milk.

recipes.name: Cold sesame noodle salad with salmon, edamame and crunchy veg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese cold sesame noodles, with whole-wheat spaghetti and canned salmon
recipes.about: Whole-wheat noodles tossed in a soy, rice vinegar and sesame dressing with edamame, carrot, red pepper and kale, topped with flaked canned salmon. The salmon (soft bones and all) brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the edamame adds protein and folate.

ingredients.note: whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles
washed, stems removed, very thinly sliced
washed and cut into thin matchsticks
washed and cut into thin strips

steps: Boil the whole-wheat spaghetti (the noodles) in plenty of water until tender with a little bite, about 10 minutes. Add the frozen edamame for the last 3 minutes so it is steaming hot all the way through, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil and grated ginger in a large bowl.

Wash the carrot, red pepper, kale and scallion, then cut the carrot into matchsticks, the pepper into thin strips and slice the kale and scallion very thinly. Flake the salmon with a fork, keeping the soft bones.
Toss the noodles, edamame and vegetables in the dressing and let the kale soften for 5 minutes. Top with the salmon and sesame seeds.
Eat it the same day. If you pack it for lunch, keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack. Keep an opened tin of salmon covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Beef and egg lo mein with bok choy, carrot and edamame
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American lo mein, with whole-wheat spaghetti as the noodles
recipes.about: Chewy whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles, tossed in a hot wok with strips of lean beef, firm egg ribbons, bok choy, carrot, garlic and a savoury soy and vinegar sauce. The beef, egg and edamame bring **protein, iron and choline**, and a big pile of bok choy and carrot keeps the noodle portion modest.

ingredients.note: whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles
washed and cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Boil the whole-wheat spaghetti (the noodles) in plenty of water until just tender, about 10 minutes, adding the frozen edamame for the last 3 minutes so it is steaming hot all the way through. Drain and toss with half of the sesame oil so they do not stick.
Wash the bok choy, spinach, carrot and scallion. Slice the bok choy and scallion and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks. Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chili flakes in a small bowl.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Pour in the beaten egg and stir until completely set and firm, about 1 minute, then move it to a plate and break it into ribbons.

Add the beef in a single layer and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, with no pink and at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 3 minutes. Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw beef.
Add the carrot and garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute, then the bok choy and scallion for 2 minutes, until the stems are tender but still have a little crunch, and stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Return the beef and egg, add the noodles and the sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the noodles are steaming hot. Drizzle with the rest of the sesame oil, scatter over the sesame seeds and serve.
recipes.tip: Packing it for work? Cook it the night before, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep it cold with an ice pack and reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

recipes.name: Kung pao-style tofu and chickpeas with green beans and carrot over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Sichuan kung pao, with tofu and chickpeas in place of the chicken
recipes.about: Golden tofu, hearty chickpeas, crisp-tender green beans, carrot and spinach in a tangy, lightly sweet and chili-spiked sauce, finished with toasted cashews and scallion, over brown rice. The tofu and chickpeas bring **plant protein, iron and calcium**, and the brown rice keeps the portion modest.

ingredients.note: extra-firm, patted dry and cut into small cubes
washed, trimmed and cut in thirds
washed and sliced into thin coins

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Meanwhile, wash the vegetables. Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, chili flakes and 3 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl. Toast the cashews in a dry wok or skillet over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, then tip onto a plate.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Add the tofu and fry, turning, until golden on most sides, about 5 minutes. Move it to a plate.

Add a little more oil if the pan is dry, then add the green beans and carrot and stir-fry until blistered in places and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes, adding a splash of water if they start to stick. Add the garlic and scallion and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

Add the chickpeas, tofu and spinach, then stir the sauce and pour it in. Bubble, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the sauce is reduced and glossy, about 3 minutes, and everything is steaming hot.
Spoon over the rice and scatter with the cashews and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Egg and edamame fried brown rice with carrot and kale
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese vegetable fried rice
recipes.about: Brown rice stir-fried hot with firm-scrambled egg, edamame, carrot, kale, spinach and garlic, finished with soy and a little sesame oil. The egg and edamame bring **protein, choline and folate**, and the brown rice stays a modest portion.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.
Spread the drained rice on a tray in a thin layer and let it steam dry for 10 minutes. Wash the carrot, kale, spinach and scallion, dice the carrot and slice the kale and scallion.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Pour the beaten egg into the hot wok and stir until completely set and firm, about 1 minute, then move it to a plate.

Add the carrot, garlic, ginger and the white part of the scallion and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the frozen edamame straight from the freezer and stir-fry until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes.
Add the rice and the egg and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing it against the pan, until it is steaming hot and a little toasty.
Add the kale, spinach, soy sauce and chili flakes and toss until the greens wilt, about 2 minutes. Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter over the rest of the scallion and the sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Best with rice cooked and chilled the night before: cook a little extra with Friday dinner, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container, and fry it straight from the fridge (use within 3 days) for a quick lunch.

recipes.name: Chicken and cashew stir-fry with red pepper, carrot and spinach over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American cashew chicken
recipes.about: Tender chicken, toasted cashews, red pepper, carrot and spinach in a savoury garlic-ginger sauce, spooned over brown rice. The cashews bring **magnesium, zinc and copper**, and the carrot and red pepper bring **vitamin A and C**.

ingredients.note: washed and sliced into thin coins

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and broth together in a bowl. Toast the cashews in a dry wok or skillet over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, then tip onto a plate.
Wash the red pepper, carrot, spinach and scallion, then cut them as described in the list. Pat the chicken dry.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.

Add the chicken in a single layer (in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam) and let it sear for 1 minute, then stir-fry until golden and cooked through, with no pink inside and 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 5 minutes a batch. Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Add the carrot and a splash of water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the red pepper, garlic, ginger and scallion for 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.

Return the chicken and add the spinach, then stir the sauce and pour it in. Bubble, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the sauce has bubbled down to a few spoonfuls that coat everything, about 2 minutes. Toss in half of the cashews and the sesame seeds.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: Keep the other half of the cashews in a jar and stir them into the second portion when you reheat it, so they stay crunchy.

recipes.name: Orange-garlic salmon with stir-fried bok choy, kale and carrot over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese orange-flavoured fish and greens, pan-seared at home
recipes.about: A seared salmon fillet glazed with fresh orange juice, garlic and black pepper, over brown rice with bok choy, kale and carrot stir-fried in garlic. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the greens, carrot and orange bring calcium, vitamin K, vitamin A and vitamin C.

ingredients.note: skin-on fillet, fresh and used within a day of buying
washed and cut into thin ribbons or coins
washed, halved and squeezed for the juice

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Stir the orange juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar, black pepper and half of the garlic together in a small bowl. Wash the bok choy, kale and carrot, then cut the bok choy into chunks, tear the kale and cut the carrot into thin ribbons or coins. Pat the salmon dry.

Warm half of the canola oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay in the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes until the skin is crisp, then flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily and the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F).

Pour the orange mixture into the pan for the last minute, turning the salmon once, until it bubbles down into a sticky glaze. Lift the salmon onto a clean plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.

Wipe out the pan and heat the rest of the oil over high heat until it shimmers. Stir-fry the carrot for 3 minutes, then add the kale, bok choy and the rest of the garlic and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the kale has wilted and the stems are crisp-tender.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the greens alongside. Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter over the sesame seeds.

recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American beef and broccoli, with a garlicky black pepper sauce
recipes.about: Thin slices of lean sirloin, bright broccoli, kale and bok choy in a savoury, garlicky black pepper sauce, over brown rice. The beef and greens bring **iron, zinc and vitamin C** together, so the iron absorbs well, and the kale and bok choy add calcium.

ingredients.note: washed and cut into small florets
whites and greens, cut into 4 cm pieces

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Stir the cornstarch into the cold broth until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar and black pepper. Wash the broccoli, kale, bok choy and scallion, then cut them as described in the list.

Pat the beef dry. Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, add half of the oil and swirl until it shimmers, then sear the beef in a single layer (in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam) for 2 minutes a batch, stirring, until browned and cooked through with no pink and at least 71 °C (160 °F). Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw beef.

Add the rest of the oil, then the scallion and stir-fry until softened and lightly browned, about 2 minutes. Add the broccoli, garlic and a splash of water, cover for 1 minute, then add the kale and bok choy and stir-fry until the broccoli is bright green and crisp-tender and the greens have wilted, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef to the pan, stir the sauce again and pour it in. Bubble for 1 minute, stirring, until glossy. Stir in the sesame oil and scatter over the sesame seeds.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.

recipes.name: Garlic shrimp and snow peas with carrot and bok choy over whole-wheat noodles
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Cantonese shrimp with snow peas in a light white garlic sauce
recipes.about: Plump shrimp, crisp snow peas, sweet carrot and bok choy in a light, glossy garlic-ginger sauce over whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles. The shrimp bring **lean protein, iodine and selenium**, and the snow peas bring vitamin C.

ingredients.note: whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles
peeled, deveined, thawed in the fridge if frozen
washed and sliced thinly on the diagonal

steps: Boil the whole-wheat spaghetti (the noodles) in plenty of water until just tender, about 10 minutes, then drain and toss with the sesame oil.

Meanwhile, stir the cornstarch into the cold broth until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce. Wash the snow peas, carrot, bok choy and scallion, then cut them as described in the list. Pat the shrimp dry.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, then add the bok choy and snow peas for 2 minutes. Push the vegetables to the side.

Add the shrimp, garlic and ginger and stir-fry until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through (70 °C / 158 °F), about 3 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw shrimp.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens, turns glossy and coats the shrimp. Fold in the scallion.
Spoon over the noodles, scatter over the sesame seeds and serve straight away.
recipes.tip: Shrimp turn rubbery when they sit, so this one is best eaten the day it is cooked.

recipes.name: Garlic-chili tofu with kale, bok choy and carrot over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Sichuan-style home-cooked tofu with greens
recipes.about: Golden pan-crisped tofu and a big pile of kale, bok choy and carrot in a garlicky, lightly spicy sauce, over brown rice. The tofu brings **plant protein, calcium and iron**, and the greens and carrot bring vitamin K, folate and vitamin A.

ingredients.note: extra-firm, patted dry and cut into cubes
washed and sliced into thin coins

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Press the tofu between clean towels for 10 minutes, then cut it into cubes. Stir the cornstarch into 4 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey and chili flakes.
Wash the kale, bok choy, carrot and scallion, then tear the kale, slice the bok choy and scallion and cut the carrot into thin coins.

Warm half of the oil in a nonstick wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, until golden and crisp on most sides, about 8 minutes, in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam. Move it to a plate.

Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic, ginger and scallion and stir for 20 seconds. Add the carrot and kale with a splash of water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the bok choy and stir-fry 2 minutes more, until tender with a little crunch.
Return the tofu, stir the sauce again and pour it in. Bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until glossy, clinging to the tofu and hot all the way through. Stir in the sesame oil.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: The tofu softens as it sits. Give the second portion 2 minutes in a hot skillet to bring back some crispness.

recipes.name: Sweet and sour shrimp with pineapple, red pepper and bok choy over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American sweet and sour shrimp, stir-fried instead of deep-fried
recipes.about: Plump shrimp, red pepper, bok choy, scallion and pineapple in a bright, tangy tomato and pineapple sauce with no deep-frying, over brown rice. The pepper, tomato and pineapple bring **vitamin C**, and the shrimp bring lean protein and iodine.

ingredients.note: peeled, deveined, thawed in the fridge if frozen
peeled, cored and cut into chunks

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Stir the cornstarch into 4 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, then stir in the rice vinegar and soy sauce. Pat the shrimp dry. Wash the pepper, tomato, bok choy and scallion and cut them as described in the list.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.

Add the pepper, scallion and garlic and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the bok choy, tomato and pineapple for 2 minutes, until the vegetables are crisp-tender and the tomato just starts to break down.
Return the shrimp, stir the sauce again and pour it in. Bubble, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes until it turns glossy and coats the shrimp.
Spoon over the rice and serve.

recipes.name: Sesame-crusted salmon with garlicky green beans over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese sesame-crusted fish and garlicky green beans
recipes.about: A pan-seared salmon fillet pressed with toasted sesame seeds, served with blistered garlic-ginger green beans in a splash of soy and rice vinegar, over brown rice. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the green beans add fibre and vitamin K.

ingredients.note: skin-on fillet, fresh and used within a day of buying

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and half of the ginger together in a small bowl. Wash the green beans and trim them. Pat the salmon dry and press the sesame seeds onto the flesh side.

Warm half of the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay in the salmon seed-side down and cook for 3 minutes until the seeds are golden and toasty, then flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until opaque and flaking and the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Lift the salmon onto a clean plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.

Wipe the pan, add the rest of the oil and heat over high heat until it shimmers. Stir-fry the green beans until blistered in places and crisp-tender, 5 to 6 minutes, adding the garlic and the rest of the ginger for the last minute and a splash of water to steam them through, then pour in the soy mixture for the last 30 seconds.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the green beans and drizzle with the sesame oil.

steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Pear with walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy pear with a small handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **omega-3 fats and fibre**, and the pear brings sweetness and more fibre.

recipes.name: Carrot and red pepper sticks with ginger-soy yogurt dip
recipes.about: Crunchy carrot and red pepper sticks with a quick Greek yogurt dip spiked with ginger and a little soy. The carrot brings **vitamin A**, the pepper vitamin C, and the yogurt protein and calcium.
steps: Stir the yogurt, grated ginger, soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl.
Wash the carrot and red pepper, cut them into sticks and dip. Keep the dip in the fridge and finish it the same day.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with garlic and chili
recipes.about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with garlic, a little soy and chili flakes. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat the edamame in a pan with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar and chili flakes and eat warm.

recipes.about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with toasted sesame seeds, fresh ginger and a splash of soy. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**, and the sesame adds crunch.

recipes.about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with sesame seeds, a pinch of chili and a little soy. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and iron**, and the sesame adds crunch.

ingredients.note: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the very dry chickpeas with the oil, soy sauce, sesame seeds and chili flakes on a small baking tray.
Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp, about 25 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes and eat the same day.

ingredients.note: washed, peeled and cut into segments

recipes.name: Firm-boiled egg with soy-ginger dip and red pepper strips
recipes.about: A firm-boiled egg with crunchy red pepper strips and a little soy and ginger to dip. The egg brings **protein and choline**, and the red pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Lower the egg into a small pot of boiling water and cook for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold running water and peel it.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and grated ginger together for the dip. Wash the red pepper, cut it into strips and serve with the egg.

recipes.name: Pineapple and pear with fresh ginger
recipes.about: Juicy pineapple and pear tossed with a little grated fresh ginger, a bright, sweet snack with no cooking. It brings **vitamin C and fibre**.

ingredients.note: peeled, cored and cut into chunks

steps: Wash the pear and the pineapple before cutting. Peel, core and cut the pineapple into chunks and slice the pear.
Toss with the grated ginger and eat right away, or pack it in a lidded tub in the fridge and eat it the same day.
